newsitem.title: USA: Exxon targets former Soviet Union, Africa.
newsitem.headline: Exxon targets former Soviet Union, Africa.

text.p: Exxon Corp said on Monday that it was in exclusive negotiations with governments of the former Soviet Union to acquire an additional 20 billion barrels of oil equivalent to its reserve portfolio.

"We already have rights to in excess of 10 billion barrels and are in exclusive negotiations on an additional 10 billion," company chief executive Lee Raymond told the annual Howard Weil energy conference in New Orleans.
Included in the figure are exclusive talks on additional offshore acreage in Azerbaijan.

The company forecasts that two-thirds of global energy demand of 150 million barrels of oil equivalent needed by the year 2010 will have to come from new discoveries and these will primarily be outside the U.S.

Exxon already participates in the Sakhalin One field in the Russian Far East, where it has a 30 percent share of a five billion barrel of oil equivalent field, and Sakhalin Three, where it has a one hundred percent working interest.
"There are two billion barrels of reserves in Sakhalin Three and we are awaiting government approval and have already negotiated production sharing agreements," Raymond said.
Elsewhere in Russia, Raymond said Exxon has negotiated a production sharing agreement for Timan Pechora block in Sibera, where there are 11 discovered fields with one billion barrels of reserves.
Exxon also expects to conclude a production sharing agreement with Russian authorities for the Reef Trend area within a year.
Reserves there are 600 million barrels of oil equivalent.
Raymond expects production from the five billion barrel Azeri Megastructure field to start in 1997 and forecasts peak production of 800,000 barrels per day.
In Kazakhstan, Exxon expects to start drilling an exploratory well in 1997 on its three million acre concession.
In Africa, Raymond said that Exxon had made two discoveries from three blocks off the shore of Angola.
"We could see oil by the year 2000 from one of these," Raymond said.
Exxon is due to start drilling offshore Congo where it has three blocks and is also targeting the Chad Doha field, where Raymond said that development costs would be $3.0 billion.
Exxon has a 40 percent stake in Doha.
